Our actual results could differ materially from the results anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors including those set forth under "Risk Factors," beginning at page 14 and elsewhere in this Form 10-K. Although we believe that the expectations reflected in the forward-looking statements are reasonable, we cannot guarantee future results, levels of activity, performance or achievements. You should not place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements. We disclaim any obligation to update information contained in any forward-looking statement. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: When evaluating Microchip and its business, you should give careful consideration to the factors below, as well as the information provided elsewhere in this Form 10-K and in other filings we make with the SEC. Risk Factor Summary Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry • impact of global economic conditions on our operating results, net sales and profitability; • impact of economic conditions on the financial viability and performance of our licensees, customers, distributors, or suppliers; • impact of supplier disruptions affecting the availability and cost of raw materials, components, or equipment; • impact of restrictions, export controls, or other limitations on critical materials sourced from concentrated suppliers reducing sales; • dependence on wafer foundries and other contractors by our licensees and ourselves; • dependence on foreign sales, suppliers, and operations, which exposes us to foreign political and economic risks; • impact of geopolitical instability in the Middle East on the availability of critical semiconductor materials, fuel costs, and our ability to meet customer demand; • dependence on orders received and shipped in the same quarter, limited visibility to product shipments other than those shipped through our certain LTSAs; • intense competition in the markets we serve, leading to pricing pressures, reduced sales or market share; • ability to introduce new products on a timely basis, including in response to market changes driven by AI and other factors, or by changing our product design and manufacturing to more advanced technology nodes; • ineffective utilization of our manufacturing capacity or failure to maintain manufacturing yields; • impact of seasonality and wide fluctuations of supply and demand in the industry; • dependence on distributors; • business interruptions affecting our operations or that of key vendors, licensees or customers; • technology licensing business exposes us to various risks; • the impact of the effects of sustained adverse climate change on our operations; • reliance on sales into governmental projects, and compliance with associated regulations; • risks related to grants from, or tax arrangements with, governments, agencies and research organizations; • ability to realize anticipated benefits from completed or future acquisitions or divestitures; • future impairments to goodwill or intangible assets; • our failure to maintain proper and effective internal control and remediate future control deficiencies; • customer demands to implement business practices that are more stringent than legal requirements; • ability to attract and retain qualified personnel; and • the occurrence of events for which we are self-insured, or which exceed our insurance limits. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers capital spending and dividends, with free cash flow comfortably exceeding the annual distribution, so internal liquidity funds the payout without incremental borrowing. The cash conversion cycle remains a core funding source, and the current ratio sits above the sector median, indicating solid near-term liquidity headroom.

The debt stack is entirely senior unsecured with no secured claims, and the revolving facility is undrawn, leaving committed backup liquidity available. Convertible notes carry very low coupons, and the commercial paper programme provides flexible short-term funding at a modest balance relative to the total debt outstanding.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage flags dependence on wafer foundries and subcontractors, concentrated critical-material suppliers, and export controls or tariffs, particularly those impacting China. Any supply disruption or trade restriction could compress revenue and margins, weakening the cash flow available to service the substantial debt load.

The debt note shows a large convertible maturity inside the next twelve months alongside a sizeable senior note maturity in year two, with the convertible principal excluded from current maturities only because the company intends to refinance via the revolver. Refinancing depends on continued revolver access and market conditions.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is thin relative to the sector median, and leverage sits well above the sector median, placing the indicative financial risk profile in the aggressive tier. Headroom to the next leverage threshold is limited, so a modest EBITDA decline or incremental debt could push the profile lower.

Free cash flow to debt is weak versus the sector median, and cash on hand is small relative to the debt stack, so servicing relies on recurring operating cash flow. The maturity profile concentrates repayments in the next few years, requiring refinancing or sustained cash generation to avoid liquidity strain.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer is a semiconductor supplier with a leveraged balance sheet, weak interest coverage and free cash flow to debt well below sector norms. The indicative financial risk profile is aggressive, and the maturity wall over the next few years concentrates refinancing needs, making credit quality sensitive to demand and pricing trends.

Our forward view is that leverage remains elevated unless EBITDA recovers or debt is reduced, and the dividend absorbs most free cash flow, limiting deleveraging. We would monitor refinancing of the near-term convertible and senior maturities, supply-chain and tariff developments, and any deterioration in operating cash flow as key credit drivers.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支及股息，自由現金流穩健地超過年度分派，因此內部流動性可為派息提供資金而無需額外借貸。現金轉換週期仍是核心資金來源，而流動比率高於行業中位數，顯示短期流動性緩衝穩健。
債務結構全為優先無抵押，並無有抵押索償，而循環信貸額度尚未動用，留有已承諾的備用流動性。可換股票據票息極低，而商業票據計劃提供靈活的短期資金，相對於未償還債務總額，結餘溫和。

key_risks.text: 風險因素段落指出依賴晶圓代工廠及分包商、關鍵材料供應商集中，以及出口管制或關稅，尤其是影響中國的措施。任何供應中斷或貿易限制均可能壓縮收入及利潤率，削弱可用於償付龐大債務的現金流。
債務附註顯示未來十二個月內有一筆大額可換股到期，同時第二年有一筆規模可觀的優先票據到期，可換股本金僅因公司擬透過循環信貸再融資而排除於流動到期項之外。再融資取決於能否持續獲得循環信貸及市場狀況。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率相對於行業中位數偏薄，而槓桿遠高於行業中位數，使指示性財務風險狀況處於進取級別。距離下一個槓桿門檻的緩衝有限，因此EBITDA溫和下降或債務增加可能將狀況推低。
自由現金流對債務比率相對於行業中位數疲弱，而手頭現金相對於債務結構規模偏小，因此償付依賴經常性營運現金流。到期結構將還款集中於未來數年，需要再融資或持續現金產生以避免流動性壓力。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人為半導體供應商，資產負債表槓桿高，利息覆蓋率疲弱，自由現金流對債務比率遠低於行業常規。指示性財務風險狀況為進取，而未來數年的到期牆集中再融資需求，使信貸質素對需求及定價趨勢敏感。
我們的前瞻觀點是，除非EBITDA回升或債務減少，否則槓桿將維持高企，而股息吸收大部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿。我們將監察近期可換股及優先票據到期的再融資、供應鏈及關稅發展，以及營運現金流的任何惡化，作為關鍵信貸驅動因素。
